meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.text: 村西監督、テレビ出演おめでとう！
examples.trans: Director Muranishi, congratulations on your television appearance!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 村西さん、テレビ出禁なんだろ？
examples.trans: I hear Muranishi got banned from television, didn't he?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: ファンが怒ることで宣伝になるんだからすげえよな。
examples.trans: Turning angry fans into free publicity is pretty wild, I'll give him that.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.

examples.text: 古谷さんと手組んで、うちの作品を裏で流す。
examples.trans: Team up with Furuya and distribute our films underground.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Polite presumptive form of copula だ; with rising intonation, seeks agreement.

examples.text: 明日は晴れるでしょう。
examples.trans: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: ああ、何だ、びっくりした。彼女は？
examples.trans: Oh, come on, you startled me. Then where is she?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 五日で十五本撮りって新記録っすよね。
examples.trans: Shooting fifteen videos in five days has got to be a new record.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

examples.text: そうです。この巨大アンテナから飛んだ電波を衛星がキャッチするんです。
examples.trans: That's right. Orbiting satellites catch the waves beamed from these giant antennas.

examples.text: そして今度は衛星から地球に電波が降り注ぐ。
examples.trans: And then the signals shower back down from the satellite onto the earth.

examples.text: もちろん。そのための衛星だ。
examples.trans: Of course. That is what the satellite is for.

examples.text: 監督は今は衛星にご執心ですけど、また撮れる日を楽しみにしてるんです。
examples.trans: He is absorbed in satellites right now, yet I look forward to the day we film again.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.
Softens a refusal or correction at the start of a reply.
